newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - NZ Business weeklies - April 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - NZ Business weeklies - April 18.

text.p: Sir Howard bids to save Cook Is: Sir Howard Morrison is in the Cook Islands trying to resuscitate the government's abandoned Sheraton hotel project by buying the multi-million dollar complex himself. Page 1.

Court hears details of Pacer share-go-round: Fallen business tycoon David Phillips used a Cook Islands share register as a device to conceal secret cash-generating share transactions, the High Court at Auckland has heard. Page 1.
Norm to storm NBR forum: Stormin' Norman has joined ranks with business legend Lee Iacocca to address The National Business Review World Masters of Business leadership event in August. Page 1.

Directors quit after hi-tech firm's boardroom battle: Food technology developer QPod Systems has lost three directors after a disagreement with chief executive and controlling shareholder Paul Bosher. Page 2.

TV news cleared in contempt case but judges urge caution: The networks' court victory shows judicial sympathy for media freedom: The court victory by TV3 and TVNZ over the right to broadcast graphic footage of the mayhem caused by a deranged motorist does not represent a watering-down of the contempt law. Page 5.
Poor probes the result of SFO infighting -- Goff: Internal politics at the Serious Fraud Office may be undermining the quality of its investigations Labour justice spokesman Phil Goff says. Page 9.

Trade 'ban' just storm in teacup: This week's Iran trade ban scare occurred because New Zealand broke the cardinal rule of diplomatic relations with super sensitive countries: Don't take them by surprise. Page 10.

Government promises advice on good and bad funds managers: The government would indicate to the public which were the good and the bad managers of superannuation schemes, Treasurer Winston Peters has told the Wellington chapter of the Association of Investment Advisers and Financial Plannes. Page

Bolger says super unsustainable but taskforce, NZIER disagree: Prime Minister Jim Bolger told the American Chamber of Commerce on Wednesday that the current system of superannuation was unsustainable. Page 11.

Auckland City pulls Fay out of the pool: After running the Tepid Baths for more than ten years, John Fay, brother of Sir Michael and developer of the Newmarket Olympic Pool, has been given his marching orders by the Auckland City Council. Page 11.

Kiwis are tucking money into retirement piggybanks: New Zealanders are thinking more about providing for their retirement says a report, the Westpac FPG Household Savings Indicators, released this week. Page 11.

Review application may delay wine-box report: Extension granted inquiry commissioner givers merchant bank time to get court backing for its objection: The extension granted this week to wine-box commissioner Sir Ronald Davison to report his findings is an 11th-hour bonus for merchant banker Fay Richwhite
New law means taxman may target bikie gangs: Inland Revenue is adamant it has the powers to bust any New Zealand imitator of famed US gangster Al Capone. Page 13.

All Blacks Club abandoned: Rugby's PR trimph last season has not helped save the game's main marketing spin-off. This season the sickly All Blacks Club joins the Rugby Hall of Fame on the sports club scrap heap. Page 13.

Cave Creek prosecution urged: Parents of dead youngsters want police investigation of Doc staff reopened: A parent of one of the Cave Creek victims has called for the reopening of the police investigation into those responsible for the tragedy. Page 14.
